summary.tldr: Sets rules provinces must meet for federal cash contributions to public drug insurance plans.
what_it_does: Sets five conditions for provincial drug plans to qualify for federal cash contributions: public administration, comprehensiveness, universality, portability and accessibility.
Requires public drug plans to cover all insured prescription drugs and related dispensing fees for insured persons on uniform terms.
Limits residence or waiting periods to no more than three months and sets rules for drug coverage when insured persons travel or move between provinces.
Allows the Minister of Health to ask provinces for information, then refer non-compliance to the Governor in Council, which may reduce or withhold payments.
Lets the federal government and provinces create an independent drug agency to assess drugs, advise on coverage, negotiate prices and monitor safety.
Requires the Minister of Health to table an annual report in Parliament on how provinces met the bill's criteria and conditions.
summary.background: The bill applies to cash contributions that may be provided to a province under other Acts of Parliament. It defines a drug insurance plan as a provincial plan or plans that cover the cost of insured drugs and related dispensing fees.
